summary: Chelan County, WA L-4 lookout on a knob in the Wenatchee National Forest, built in the 1930s and now gone; concrete footings are reported, reached by a short walk from the Soda Springs Campground road.

facts.design: L-4 tower (register); Willhite reports an L-4 cab and estimates a tower about 30 feet tall from the 1934 panorama height
facts.status_note: Register and Firelookout.com say the tower is gone; footings were reported by a 2009 trip report and in Willhite's photos

visit.trail_note: Park at the Soda Springs Campground entrance road and walk through open woods around the base of the knob, about a quarter mile with 150 feet of gain. Cross signs mark a National Forest and private land boundary about halfway up. Willhite warns against continuing south toward a large rock quarry

events.note: Panorama photos taken August 24, 1934, reportedly from about 45 feet; Willhite infers a tower of about 30 feet. Year of construction not given; the register says the 1930s
Trip report (22 Aug 2009) finds four concrete foundation blocks on a rocky knoll
Willhite photo captions, some labeled September 2017, describe footings

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse with the Gifford Pinchot 'Soda Spring Campground' page (Cowlitz Valley, Forest Road 4510.052), which is a different place and was not used. No construction year is given; 1934 is only the earliest dated record, so it appears only as the earliest dated record. No staffing or fire history appears in the sources read. Access level is left out because no source says whether the knob is public. Footings rest on a 2009 trip report and Willhite's photos.
